chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I have a cousin whom I maintain kinship with, but he cuts me off; and I maintain kinship with him, but he cuts me off. To the extent that I have contemplated cutting him off in response to his cutting me off. Do you permit me to cut him off?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you maintain it to him and he cuts you off, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, maintains it with both of you together. And if you cut him off and he cuts you off, Allah will cut off both of you.'

key_terms.وَصَلَكُمَا اللَّهُ: Allah maintains [the bond] for you both

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on maintaining kinship when the relative cuts you off?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the specific dilemma of unilateral kinship maintenance (silat al-rahim) where one party remains steadfast despite the other's severance. The Imam distinguishes between divine reciprocity in mutual severance versus the enduring spiritual bond and divine mercy granted to the one who perseveres in goodness, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence regarding family ties. This teaching emphasizes that the reward for maintaining kinship is not contingent upon the other's response, but rather on the individual's fidelity to God's command.
